localChanges: Computer players now set their own tax, luxury and science rates to suit their leader's personality, as in Civ1, instead of sitting at 50/50 for the whole game (#154).
A computer player stops researching once it knows Robotics and every advance its leader still wants, and puts that income into its treasury instead (#155).
Long games are much faster: reaching turn 400 with four computer players took over nine minutes and now takes under one (#217).

The `disembark` action's criterion asked "is this unit aboard anything?" by calling `transportRegistry.getByUnit` inside a `try`. The answer is nearly always "no", and `getByUnit` gives that answer by constructing a `TypeError`, stack trace included. The criterion runs for every tile beside every unit whose actions are listed, which the AI does for each neighbour of each step it considers. `movementCost.ts` made the same change in 0.1.5.

Seed 1, without checksums (civ-clone/web-renderer#217): turns 300-400 spent 1.8s of about 57s constructing those errors. 400 turns, measured back-to-back with the other #217 fixes in both arms: 62.7s / 62.0s before, 60.8s / 60.8s after.

`hasUnit` is true for one manifest or more where `getByUnit` needs exactly one. They differ only for a unit stowed twice, which stowing and unloading cannot produce; there the next criterion's `getByUnit` would throw instead.
Play is unchanged: the conformance documents at turns 1, 10, 50 and 150 are identical, and so are the state digest and RNG draw count at 150, 200, 250 and 300.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#217

`getByTile` filtered a copy of every city to find the one on a tile. The AI asks it of every tile a player knows each turn, and of the 81 tiles around every candidate city site, and the movement and action rules ask it too. A city's tile is fixed for its lifetime (capture changes its player, not its tile), so the `index()` from core-registry 0.1.3 keeps it current with no `reindex`; destroyed cities are still filtered out. The range moves to `^0.1.3` accordingly.

Copied from core-strategy: Node 22 and pnpm in place of Node 12 and npm, and a compile step that fails when the committed .js, .d.ts or .js.map is stale. `prettier:check` now passes `--check`, so it fails on unformatted files rather than printing them (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

`getByTile` was `getBy('tile', tile)`: a copy of the whole registry, a bound function per improvement, and a scan, on every call. Movement-cost rules ask it for the tile a unit is leaving and the tile it is entering, for every step a unit or a path search considers, so late in a game it was asked over a million times per 100 turns of a registry holding hundreds of improvements. An improvement's tile is fixed for its lifetime (building registers it, pillaging unregisters it), so the `index()` from core-registry 0.1.3 keeps it current with no `reindex`. The range moves to `^0.1.3` accordingly.

Seed 1, AI at simple-ai-client 51b24e5, no checksums, back-to-back (civ-clone/web-renderer#217): 300 turns 69.4s / 75.1s before, 33.0s / 33.8s after. Most of the late-game cost was failed path searches, and every step of those asked this.

Play is unchanged: the conformance documents at turns 1, 10, 50 and 150 are identical, and so are the state digest and RNG draw count at 150, 200, 250 and 300. The package gets its first tests, for the index's ordering, removal and copy semantics.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#217

`claimSite` tried every site on the board, nearest first, until `Path.for` found a path. A site on another continent has none, and finding that out is a uniform-cost search over the worker's whole continent. Once ships have shown the players other coasts, most of the board can be such sites, and every worker without a site searched for each of them every turn. It now checks the site against `reachableTiles` first, as `pursue` has done since #12.
Seed 1, measured without checksums (civ-clone/web-renderer#217):
turns 250-300: 52.7s, of which 39.7s was 5,350 `claimSite` searches, 5,339 of them failed; with this change 16.2s.
400 turns: 560s before, about 90s after.

Play is unchanged. The conformance checksums at turns 1, 10, 50 and 150 are identical, and the engine state digest and RNG draw count are identical at turns 150, 200, 250 and 300. The DTO digest at turn 150 moves, and only in the ids of `Move` actions and `Movement` yields: each skipped search would have created some, and those ids come from per-class counters.

`surveyTargets` asked `unitRegistry.getBy('tile', tile)` for every tile the player knows, every turn. Each call copies the whole unit registry and binds a function per unit, so by turn 400 (about 1,500 known tiles each, 400 units) the survey alone made over two million unit comparisons per player per turn. It now builds a tile-to-units map in one pass over the registry, keeping the destroyed units that `getBy` included, and reads that.

Seed 1, 400 turns, without checksums, measured back-to-back with the reachability fix and the core-tile-improvement / core-city indexes in both arms (civ-clone/web-renderer#217): 69.6s / 69.3s before, 62.7s / 62.0s after.

Play is unchanged: the conformance documents at turns 1, 10 and 50 are identical, the checksums at 150 are identical, and the state digest and RNG draw count are identical at turns 150, 200, 250 and 300.

A `TradeRates` strategy on `AfterTurn`, registered straight after `PreventDisorder`, sets each computer player's rates for the turn ahead with v474.05's routine (OpenCivOne `F0_1ade_0006`), so the AI no longer plays the whole game at 50/50/0. `lib/tradeRates.ts` is the routine as a pure function in tenths; `lib/traits.ts` gives Mood, Policy and Ideology (-1/0/1) from the leader's traits, looked up by leader class in the game's `TraitRegistry`, with Militarism flipped so Civilized is +1.

On a player's first turn the rates start at Ideology + 3 science and 1 luxury. A city `PreventDisorder` left uncalmed for `food` or `tiles` adds one luxury step (`growth` cities don't), and when the luxury rate changes every city is calmed again. Civ1's policy reads disorder from the `CIVIL_DISORDER` pending effect and takes a city larger than 5 with as many happy citizens as unhappy ones to be on the edge.

One departure from v474.05, `LUXURY_REDUCTION_BELOW`: a luxury is taken away every 4th turn while science + tax < 10, not < 8, so luxuries fall back to 0 when nothing needs them. The original rule kept 1 or 2 luxuries for good and cost 2.8 advances and 92 gold a player over 150 turns in the arena, for no less disorder.
`Dependencies` gains `playerTradeRatesRegistry` and `traitRegistry`.

civ-clone/web-renderer#154's scope has `scienceStopped` follow v474.05 until #155 makes it personal: science 0 once the player has Robotics. Civ1's `TradeRatePolicy` now reads that from the player's research instead of always answering `false`. No 150-turn game reaches Robotics, so play is unchanged.

v474.05 sets every AI's science to 0 once it has Robotics. A player now stops only once it has every advance its leader wants (`lib/Science/wantedAdvances.ts`, by the ruleset's `WantedAdvancesPolicy`), and Civ1's `TradeRatePolicy.scienceStopped` reads that instead of Robotics alone.

Civ1's table (`lib/Civ1/wantedAdvances.ts`) is keyed by trait class: Robotics always; Militaristic adds nothing; normal militarism and a Friendly mood add Recycling and Nuclear Power; Civilized adds those and Computers, Genetic Engineering, Space Flight, Plastics, Superconductor and Fusion Power; Aggressive adds nothing. Future Technology is never wanted.

`ChooseResearch` takes the policy and picks among the wanted advances available, if any are, in the same single random draw, so the number of draws is unchanged. Once science has stopped it still answers the engine's choice from everything available.

civ-clone/web-renderer#155 lists Recycling and Nuclear Power under normal militarism and a Friendly mood only, and Civilized as adding the six advances behind the late Wonders and the spaceship. The table had read "also" as cumulative and given every Civilized leader all nine. A Civilized leader with a normal mood (Mao Zedong) now wants Robotics and the six. Lincoln and Hammurabi, being Friendly too, still want all nine.
